metaDescription: Nemacolin, PA sits in Greene County's active Marcellus wet-gas core. We buy mineral and royalty interests directly, with a full title and lease review.
heroLead: Nemacolin takes its name from the same trail that once cut through this part of southwestern Pennsylvania long before anyone imagined shale gas thousands of feet below.
intro: This Greene County community grew up around coal, and the mineral history under the surrounding land often reflects that, with old coal transactions sitting alongside newer Marcellus leases on the same tracts. If your family holds an interest here, understanding which agreement covers which depth matters for figuring out what you actually own.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Nemacolin directly. We handle the title research ourselves and give you a plain explanation of what we find.

sections.heading: Greene County's Wet-Gas Development
paragraphs: Southern Greene County, including the area around Nemacolin, has seen sustained Marcellus development for well over a decade, with multi-well pads pulling acreage from smaller legacy tracts into larger horizontal units. This is core wet-gas territory, meaning liquids revenue and processing deductions both factor into your net royalty.
If your interest has been part of a unit since the early Marcellus years, we'll look at the full production history rather than judging off recent statements alone.

sections.heading: Old Coal Transactions and Current Gas Rights
paragraphs: We research your chain of title through the Greene County Recorder of Deeds in Waynesburg, checking specifically for coal-era reservation language that might affect how your current oil and gas interest reads.
In our experience, Nemacolin-area title work often benefits from checking both current county records and older company-era conveyances together.

sections.heading: Reading Your Lease Against the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act
paragraphs: We'll compare your lease's deduction language against Pennsylvania's one-eighth royalty floor so you understand exactly where your specific agreement stands before we discuss a number.

faqs.question: Does Nemacolin's coal history affect my gas mineral rights?
faqs.answer: It can, since coal was frequently severed separately in this region. We check your specific deed history rather than assuming.

faqs.question: How active is drilling near Nemacolin right now?
faqs.answer: We evaluate current activity specific to your parcel's unit as part of our review, since it can vary even within southern Greene County.

faqs.question: What if my lease predates the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act?
faqs.answer: We'll review your specific lease terms against current law and explain what protections do or don't apply before discussing a purchase.

faqs.question: My family's interest traces back to Nemacolin's Path era. Does that history matter for title?
faqs.answer: It doesn't affect modern mineral rights directly, but very old land grants in this area sometimes use unusual boundary language, which we account for during title research.

faqs.question: What documents help speed up the review?
faqs.answer: Your deed, any lease you or a relative signed, and recent royalty statements if available are the most useful starting point for us.
